tampines.name: Tampines
tampines.text: Tampines is one of the biggest and most self-contained towns in the east, and rooms here move fast because of it. A common room typically goes for roughly $700 to $900 a month, with master rooms usually landing around $900 to $1,200, depending on renovation and whether it's aircon-equipped. Tampines East and Tampines West MRT sit on the Downtown Line, while Tampines proper connects to the East-West Line, so the ride into Raffles Place or the CBD generally runs about 35 to 45 minutes. The town suits a broad mix of tenants: professionals working in the east or commuting into the city, students at nearby polytechnics, and small families needing extra space near good schools. Tampines Mall, Tampines Hub, and IKEA keep daily life easy without leaving the area.

bedok.name: Bedok
bedok.text: Bedok is a well established east side town with a huge stock of HDB flats, which usually means more room choices at reasonable prices. Expect a common room to go for roughly $650 to $850 a month, and a master room around $850 to $1,100. Bedok MRT and Kembangan MRT sit on the East-West Line, putting the CBD roughly 30 to 40 minutes away by train. It's a popular pick for students, working professionals who want an established neighbourhood with everything already in place, and families drawn to the mix of older and newer blocks near good schools. Bedok Mall, Bedok Interchange, and the famous Bedok food centres mean amenities and hawker food are never far.

jurong-east.name: Jurong East
jurong-east.text: Jurong East is fast becoming a second CBD, so rooms here tend to sit at a slight premium for the connectivity and amenities on offer. A common room is typically around $750 to $950 a month, while a master room usually runs $950 to $1,300. Jurong East MRT is a major interchange on the East-West and North-South Lines, so commuting into the CBD generally takes about 30 to 40 minutes, and many tenants here actually work locally given the growing business hub. This makes it a strong fit for professionals employed in the Jurong Lake District, students at nearby institutions, and foreign professionals who want easy access to malls and transport. JEM, Westgate, IMM, and Jurong Lake Gardens are all within walking distance.

woodlands.name: Woodlands
woodlands.text: Woodlands sits right up in the north, and that distance from town is reflected in generally friendlier rents. A common room usually costs around $600 to $800 a month, with a master room typically $800 to $1,050. Woodlands MRT and Woodlands North MRT connect via the North-South and Thomson-East Coast Lines, and the commute into the CBD usually takes around 45 minutes to an hour, so it suits tenants who either work locally or don't mind a longer ride. Woodlands works well for families and budget conscious tenants, as well as those who frequently cross into Johor Bahru given the proximity to the Causeway. Causeway Point and several parks and schools round out the amenities.

yishun.name: Yishun
yishun.text: Yishun offers a good balance of affordability and connectivity in the north, making it a steady choice for tenants on a tighter budget. A common room typically rents for around $650 to $850 a month, while a master room is usually $850 to $1,100. Yishun MRT sits on the North-South Line, and the ride into the CBD generally takes about 40 to 50 minutes. The area suits families, professionals who don't need to be in town daily, and workers employed at nearby industrial estates like Sembawang and Woodlands. Northpoint City, Yishun Park, and a wide spread of hawker centres and clinics make day to day living convenient.

ang-mo-kio.name: Ang Mo Kio
ang-mo-kio.text: Ang Mo Kio is a mature, central-north estate with a strong supply of older flats, which usually keeps rents reasonable relative to its location. A common room typically goes for around $700 to $900 a month, with a master room around $900 to $1,150. Ang Mo Kio MRT and Yio Chu Kang MRT run on the North-South Line, putting the CBD roughly 30 to 35 minutes away, which is quicker than many outer towns. This makes it attractive to professionals who want a shorter commute without paying central rents, as well as students and families who value the established amenities. AMK Hub, Ang Mo Kio Central, and several well regarded schools are all close by.

bishan.name: Bishan
bishan.text: Bishan is a highly sought after central town, and rents here reflect that, sitting noticeably above the outer estates. A common room usually costs around $800 to $1,000 a month, and a master room typically $1,000 to $1,350. Bishan MRT is an interchange on the North-South and Circle Lines, so the CBD is generally just 20 to 25 minutes away, one of the fastest commutes on this list. That convenience makes Bishan popular with professionals who want to be close to town, as well as families drawn to its reputation for good schools. Junction 8, Bishan-Ang Mo Kio Park, and the Bishan Public Library add to its appeal.

toa-payoh.name: Toa Payoh
toa-payoh.text: Toa Payoh is one of Singapore's oldest planned towns, centrally located and well connected, which keeps demand for rooms fairly consistent. A common room typically runs around $750 to $950 a month, while a master room is usually $950 to $1,250. Toa Payoh MRT sits on the North-South Line, and the CBD is generally reachable in about 20 to 25 minutes, making it a favourite for professionals who want a short, easy commute. It also suits students and small families who appreciate the town's compact layout and long established amenities. Toa Payoh Central, HDB Hub, and a good spread of clinics, markets, and eateries are all within easy reach.

serangoon.name: Serangoon
serangoon.text: Serangoon sits in a useful middle ground, close enough to town while still offering more moderate rents than the central estates. A common room is typically around $700 to $900 a month, and a master room usually $900 to $1,200. Serangoon MRT is an interchange on the North-East and Circle Lines, with the CBD generally about 25 to 30 minutes away. This makes the area appealing to professionals and students alike, along with families who like being close to good schools and NEX mall. NEX, Serangoon Central, and the food scene around Chomp Chomp add plenty of everyday convenience.

hougang.name: Hougang
hougang.text: Hougang is a large, family friendly estate in the northeast with a wide range of flat types, which tends to keep room prices approachable. A common room usually goes for around $650 to $850 a month, with a master room typically $850 to $1,100. Hougang MRT and Kovan MRT run on the North-East Line, and the commute into the CBD generally takes about 35 to 40 minutes. It's a solid fit for families, students, and professionals who want a quieter residential feel without being too far from the city. Hougang Mall, Heartland Mall, and a strong network of parks and schools serve the area well.

sengkang.name: Sengkang
sengkang.text: Sengkang is one of the newer northeast towns, with a good number of relatively young flats, which sometimes puts rents slightly above nearby older estates. A common room typically costs around $700 to $900 a month, while a master room is usually $900 to $1,200. Sengkang MRT is served by the North-East Line and the Sengkang LRT loop, with the CBD generally about 40 minutes away. The town works well for families wanting newer housing stock, as well as professionals and students who appreciate the modern malls and facilities. Compass One, Sengkang Riverside Park, and the LRT network make getting around locally easy.

punggol.name: Punggol
punggol.text: Punggol is Singapore's newest large scale town, known for its waterfront setting and modern flats, which generally places it at the higher end of rents for an outer estate. A common room typically runs around $750 to $950 a month, and a master room usually $950 to $1,250. Punggol MRT connects via the North-East Line and the Punggol LRT, with the CBD generally around 40 to 45 minutes away, though many residents also work near the growing Punggol Digital District. This makes it attractive to young professionals, families wanting newer housing, and students at nearby institutions. Waterway Point and Punggol Waterway Park add to its draw.

clementi.name: Clementi
clementi.text: Clementi is a well connected west side town, popular with students and professionals thanks to its proximity to major universities and business parks. A common room typically costs around $750 to $950 a month, while a master room usually runs $950 to $1,250, sometimes higher near the universities. Clementi MRT sits on the East-West Line, and the CBD is generally about 25 to 30 minutes away by train. The area is especially popular with students at NUS and nearby institutions, as well as professionals working in one-north or the western business hubs. Clementi Mall, West Coast Park, and a strong cluster of eateries round out the neighbourhood.

geylang.name: Geylang
geylang.text: Geylang is a centrally located, culturally rich district known for its food scene and mixed residential character, and it tends to offer some of the more affordable rents this close to town. A common room typically goes for around $650 to $850 a month, with a master room usually $850 to $1,100. Aljunied MRT, Kallang MRT, and Paya Lebar MRT all serve the area on the East-West and Circle Lines, putting the CBD generally just 10 to 15 minutes away, among the shortest commutes on this list. This proximity makes Geylang a practical choice for professionals wanting to be close to the city on a tighter budget, and for those who work irregular hours near the area's many eateries. Its famous food streets and closeness to Paya Lebar's commercial hub are key draws.

choa-chu-kang.name: Choa Chu Kang
choa-chu-kang.text: Choa Chu Kang is a far west town that consistently ranks among the more affordable places to rent a room, largely because of the longer haul into the city. A common room typically costs around $600 to $800 a month, with a master room usually $800 to $1,050. Choa Chu Kang MRT sits on the North-South Line and also links to the Bukit Panjang LRT, with the commute into the CBD generally taking around 45 to 55 minutes. It's best suited to families and budget conscious tenants, plus students and staff at Nanyang Polytechnic and ITE College West nearby. Lot One Shoppers' Mall, Choa Chu Kang Park, and easy access to the Tengah new town keep daily needs covered.

bukit-batok.name: Bukit Batok
bukit-batok.text: Bukit Batok is a quieter west side estate wedged between nature reserves, offering a calmer, greener setting at rents below the central towns. A common room usually goes for around $650 to $850 a month, and a master room typically $850 to $1,100. Bukit Batok MRT runs on the North-South Line, and the CBD is generally about 40 to 45 minutes away by train. The town suits families who value the parks and reservoirs, tenants working in the nearby Jurong industrial and business parks, and students commuting to west side campuses. West Mall, Bukit Batok Nature Park, and the Little Guilin scenic spot are the area's main draws.

bukit-panjang.name: Bukit Panjang
bukit-panjang.text: Bukit Panjang sits near the Central Catchment Nature Reserve and has grown steadily with newer BTO projects, which keeps a decent spread of both older and newer flats available. A common room typically runs around $650 to $850 a month, while a master room is usually $850 to $1,100. Bukit Panjang MRT connects the Downtown Line with the Bukit Panjang LRT, and the CBD is generally 35 to 40 minutes away. It appeals to families wanting a green, quieter environment, professionals commuting via the Downtown Line, and tenants who want proximity to Malaysia via the nearby Woodlands and Tuas checkpoints. Hillion Mall, Bukit Panjang Plaza, and the adjoining nature reserve are the key amenities.

jurong-west.name: Jurong West
jurong-west.text: Jurong West is one of the largest HDB towns by flat count, which usually translates into a wide selection of rooms at accessible prices. A common room typically costs around $650 to $850 a month, with a master room usually $850 to $1,100. Boon Lay MRT and Pioneer MRT serve the area on the East-West Line, and the CBD is generally 40 to 50 minutes away, though many tenants here work locally given the nearby industrial parks and Nanyang Technological University. This makes it popular with NTU students and staff, factory and logistics workers, and families seeking larger, more affordable flats. Jurong Point, one of Singapore's biggest malls, along with Boon Lay Shopping Centre, anchor the area.

sembawang.name: Sembawang
sembawang.text: Sembawang is a far north town known for its laid back, small town feel and a steady stream of newer BTO flats alongside older ones. A common room typically goes for around $600 to $800 a month, and a master room usually $800 to $1,050, among the more affordable options in Singapore. Sembawang MRT sits on the North-South Line, with the CBD generally 45 minutes to an hour away, so it suits tenants who work locally or don't mind a longer commute. The town works well for families, budget conscious tenants, and those who regularly cross into Johor Bahru via the nearby Causeway. Sun Plaza, Sembawang Shopping Centre, and Sembawang Hot Spring Park round out the amenities.

pasir-ris.name: Pasir Ris
pasir-ris.text: Pasir Ris sits at the far east end of the island, known for its beach, parks, and relatively spacious flats, which keeps rents moderate for the distance from town. A common room typically runs around $650 to $850 a month, while a master room is usually $850 to $1,100. Pasir Ris MRT is on the East-West Line, and the CBD is generally about 45 minutes away, though the upcoming Cross Island Line will improve connectivity over time. It's a good fit for families who want proximity to Pasir Ris Park and the beach, as well as tenants working in the nearby Changi Business Park or at the airport. White Sands, Downtown East, and Pasir Ris Park are the main local draws.

queenstown.name: Queenstown
queenstown.text: Queenstown is one of Singapore's oldest housing estates, centrally located and increasingly popular with young professionals, so rents here sit above the outer towns. A common room typically costs around $800 to $1,000 a month, with a master room usually $1,000 to $1,350. Queenstown MRT and Redhill MRT run on the East-West Line, putting the CBD generally just 10 to 15 minutes away, one of the shortest commutes on this list. This makes Queenstown attractive to professionals working in the CBD or one-north, as well as students at nearby institutions. Queensway Shopping Centre, IKEA Alexandra, and the growing dining scene around Tiong Bahru's fringe are key conveniences.

novena.name: Novena
novena.text: Novena is a central district built around a major medical hub, and its proximity to town keeps rents on the higher side. A common room typically goes for around $850 to $1,050 a month, and a master room usually $1,050 to $1,400. Novena MRT sits on the North-South Line, with the CBD generally about 15 to 20 minutes away, making it a strong choice for professionals who prioritise a short commute. The area suits medical professionals working at Tan Tock Seng or Novena's private hospitals, along with tenants who want a central, well connected base. Square 2, United Square, and the cluster of medical centres define the neighbourhood.

bukit-timah.name: Bukit Timah
bukit-timah.text: Bukit Timah is an established, leafy district associated with landed housing and top schools, and rooms here, mostly in condos and a smaller stock of HDB flats, command a premium. A common room typically runs around $900 to $1,150 a month, while a master room usually costs $1,150 to $1,500 or more in newer condos. Beauty World MRT and King Albert Park MRT serve the area on the Downtown Line, with the CBD generally 25 to 30 minutes away. This makes Bukit Timah popular with families prioritising school proximity, expatriate tenants, and professionals who want a quieter, greener address. Beauty World Centre, Bukit Timah Nature Reserve, and a strong cluster of reputable schools are the main attractions.

marine-parade.name: Marine Parade
marine-parade.text: Marine Parade and the surrounding Katong and Joo Chiat area are known for their seaside setting and Peranakan heritage, and demand from professionals has kept rents fairly firm. A common room typically costs around $800 to $1,000 a month, with a master room usually $1,000 to $1,300. The area is currently better served by bus than MRT, though the Thomson-East Coast Line's Marine Parade and Katong Park stations have improved connectivity, with the CBD generally 20 to 25 minutes away. It suits professionals and expatriates drawn to the café and heritage shophouse scene, as well as families wanting a coastal, community feel. Parkway Parade, East Coast Park, and the Katong Joo Chiat food and retail strip are the standout amenities.

tanjong-pagar.name: Tanjong Pagar
tanjong-pagar.text: Tanjong Pagar sits right at the edge of the CBD, so rooms here, almost entirely in condos with a limited HDB pocket, are priced at a clear premium for the walk-to-work convenience. A common room typically goes for around $1,000 to $1,300 a month, and a master room usually $1,300 to $1,800 or more. Tanjong Pagar MRT and Outram Park MRT are major interchanges on the East-West, North-East, and Circle Lines, putting most of the CBD within 5 to 10 minutes on foot or one stop by train. This makes the area a strong fit for finance and legal professionals who want to minimise commute time, and expatriates who prioritise walkability over space. Tanjong Pagar Centre, Maxwell Food Centre, and the Duxton Plain area anchor the neighbourhood.
